correctness.rationale: The HSS error matrix was reconstructed from the two splitting steps. In real dimension two every skew-symmetric matrix satisfies S^2=-s^2 I, so the two skew factors become orthogonal left/right multipliers around D=(alpha I-H)(alpha I+H)^(-1), proving the exact Euclidean norm identity. For H=diag(1,2,4), alpha=2, and the explicit three-dimensional skew family, direct multiplication gives M_t e2=(-t/6,0,t/6) and the characteristic polynomial lambda(lambda^2+(t^2-2)/(9(t^2+2))). Thus the spectral radius stays at most 1/3 while the Euclidean one-step amplification diverges. Exact package replay verifies representative matrices and characteristic coefficients.

originality.rationale: The foundational HSS paper proves unconditional convergence, the Hermitian-spectrum spectral-radius upper bound, a transformed-norm contraction, and the standard bound-optimal parameter. Those results are treated as prior work. The inspected primary text does not state an ordinary Euclidean two-dimensional norm identity or a minimal-dimension transient theorem. Targeted published-record and literature searches found generic nonnormal transients and unrelated iterative-method safety boundaries but no implication-equivalent HSS result.
residual_risks: Older stationary-iteration literature may contain the same two-dimensional HSS singular-value observation under different terminology.
Generic nonnormal matrix theory contains many transient-growth constructions, although none located supplies the HSS-specific minimal-dimension statement with fixed Hermitian data.
The complex 2x2 HSS case is deliberately excluded and may behave differently because a general skew-Hermitian 2x2 matrix is not a scalar multiple of the real rotation generator.

value.rationale: A central attraction of HSS is that its classical convergence-factor bound depends only on the Hermitian part and is independent of the skew part. The finding identifies an important limit of that robustness: in the ordinary Euclidean error monitored by many users, the same fixed Hermitian data can hide arbitrarily large one-step amplification. The exact dimension-two immunity and dimension-three minimal obstruction make the distinction structural rather than a generic warning about nonnormality.
